tasks.task: Set up one-on-ones with questions for the next 8 weeks

items.when: When a manager needs a rhythm, agenda rules and questions for each person on the team
When one report needs their own meeting plan with timing and topics
When a report stays quiet, to try a warm start and questions they will enjoy answering
When the one-on-ones should tie to team goals and how decisions get settled
When the manager wants each week's prep done from last week's notes
When one-on-ones have become status updates the manager could read in a report

tasks.task: Prepare a manager for a hard feedback conversation

items.when: When a manager must say something hard and needs a script in their own voice
When you want a guided run to an opening built on facts and questions to listen with
When you want a second version that sets out what to praise and what to change
When the other person is likely to feel attacked, to try a plan that listens before it tells
When the manager keeps softening the message until it no longer says anything

tasks.task: Draft a clear, kind written feedback note

items.when: When feedback must go in writing and should change behaviour without starting a fight
When you want a firmer second draft to compare against the kind one
Before it is sent, to check the note is specific and tells the person what to do next
When the note is either too nice to be clear or too blunt to be heard

tasks.task: Help a leader ask their team for honest feedback

items.when: When a manager gives feedback but never asks for it and wants to start
When the leader needs a go-to question in their own voice and a plan for the silence
When people will not say it face to face and a short survey may work better

tasks.task: Plan a new manager's first 30 days

items.when: When someone has just become a manager and needs who to meet, what to ask and what not to promise
When the new manager must start one-on-ones in the first weeks
When they inherit an existing team and need a first message and a listening tour
When the first note to the team must say who they are and how they work
Before the plan, to map who has power and interest and how to reach each
When a new manager still acts like the best individual worker on the team

tasks.task: Plan a coaching programme of up to eight sessions

items.when: When a new client or sponsor asks for coaching and the steps need setting out
When goals are agreed and you need sessions, work between them and a way to review
At intake, when the client's goal is vague and needs focused questions to sharpen it
When the sponsor wants a group programme with a 360 form and a coaching guide
When the programme should start from skill standards and 360 feedback

tasks.task: Plan one coaching session

items.when: When one session is coming and needs a timed plan, questions, an exercise and a worksheet
When the session turns on one choice and needs questions that lead to a small step
When the exercise should be a look at where the client's week really went
When the client is overloaded and the exercise should be what to stop
When the coach wants fuller session notes without a recording bot in the call

tasks.task: Plan a group coaching or manager training session

items.when: When the session is for a group and needs timings, questions and one shared exercise
When managers must practise a skill and you need a session plan and proof of learning
When the group must practise, not listen, and each minute needs planning
When the group could coach each other, to try a peer session with rules
When people need a one-page handout to use back at their desk

tasks.task: Write messages for clients between sessions

items.when: When each gap between sessions needs a short message with a prompt and one small action
Before writing them, to compare three shapes the series of messages could take
When the action is a habit and needs a two-minute first step, a cue and a restart plan
When the client wants a weekly check-in that asks first and skips the pep talk
Before sending, to cut each message down and check it asks for one thing

tasks.task: Shape a coaching package clients understand

items.when: Before pricing, to fix what the programme includes and how long it runs
When the package needs a name, value framing, a guarantee and payment terms
When one package feels like take it or leave it, to draft three levels to compare
When the package is drafted, to score it and get the three changes that matter

tasks.task: Design a mentoring scheme with matching rules

items.when: When an employer or body decides to run a scheme, or to fix one that fizzled
When you need goals, matching rules, length and check-ins people will stick with
When you want a second design with a six-month plan and talk guides to compare
When mentoring should link to career levels and growth plans in the firm

tasks.task: Write mentor and mentee guides and session prompts

items.when: When the scheme is designed and each side needs a guide and session templates
When mentors need talk guides for each stage of the six months
When first meetings are stiff and pairs need questions that open people up
When the guides include sample feedback, to check it is specific and usable

tasks.task: Design the mentoring midpoint and end surveys

items.when: When the scheme hits its midpoint or end and needs short surveys for both sides
When you also want a focus group guide and a way to read the results
Before the survey goes out, to find leading or unclear questions
When answers are in and comments must become themes and actions with owners

tasks.task: Write launch and sign-up messages for a programme

items.when: When the scheme is ready and launch, sign-up and reminders must go out in order
When staff need a clear announcement with manager talking points and an FAQ
Before drafting, to compare three ways the invite series could run
Before the invite goes out, to score it and get subject line options
Before the messages go out, to confirm the sign-up link works and places are still open

tasks.task: Coach a manager through conflict between team members

items.when: When two people are in open conflict and the manager needs causes and a mediation plan
When the talk must stay private and needs a neutral map of the issues first
When both sides have dug in, to look for a third option after listening first
When the manager wants to rule on who is right before either side feels heard

tasks.task: Coach a leader to hand work off and keep it handed off

items.when: When the leader's week is full of work only they do and they need a handover plan
When a task is handed over and needs a one-page agreement on results, not methods
Before choosing what to hand off, to see what the week was really spent on
When the client is a founder and needs their blind spot and what only they should do
When the leader adds new work and never asks what to stop doing

tasks.task: Prepare performance, promotion and exit conversations

items.when: When the talk is about underperformance and the manager needs a script they can say
When a review is due and the manager needs it written from evidence
When someone asks for promotion and the case must be matched to the criteria
When the decision is to let someone go and it must be done fairly and told well

tasks.task: Read team health and shape how the team works

items.when: When people go quiet, burn out or leave and the leader needs findings and causes
When drive is low, to see ways to raise it through choice, skill growth and purpose
When the leader wants how the team should work written down in a short memo
When survey comments exist and need themes and actions with owners

tasks.task: Help a leader announce a change and bring the team along

items.when: When direction changes and the leader needs the memo, the script and a rollout plan
When the team's top priority must be reset in one page
When a re-org or tool switch needs message templates and a plan for pushback
Before any message, to see who the change affects and who can block it

tasks.task: Coach a leader on priorities, decisions and meetings

items.when: When a manager needs meeting rhythms and the few tasks that move the team's output
When a big decision drifts and needs one named owner and a plan to hear dissent
When the leader's meetings run long and end without owners or actions
When the team has no clear goals for the quarter and needs a few with dates and numbers
When the leader's list only grows and needs a stop list with a rule for each item

tasks.task: Report coaching progress to the sponsor

items.when: When a review point arrives and the sponsor is owed an update within agreed limits
When progress must be written up for a senior reader in a short status note
Before sending, to check the report is specific and says what happens next

always.when: When a guide or session plan cites research, to check the claim is real before it is taught

helpers.when: When a conversation touches discipline, dismissal, grievance or anything with legal risk
When coaching sits inside a wider training plan for many managers
When the client's real question is whether to stay in the role or move on
When the problem is the team's structure or roles, not one manager's skill
When a change or programme launch needs a full staff communication plan
When team health needs a proper survey run and action plan

gaps: No library item plans a one-to-one coaching programme across sessions; the nearest item designs a training programme
No library item plans a single coaching session or holds coaching questions sorted by situation
No library item writes between-session messages with a reflection prompt and one action
No library item plays the other person so a manager can rehearse a hard conversation
No library item checks a conversation script for blame, vague wording or mixed messages before it is used
No library item plans a first-time manager's first 30 days; items cover new hires or senior leaders taking over a team
No library item writes a coaching agreement with a sponsor: goals, privacy limits and review points
No library item reports coaching progress to a sponsor without breaking confidence
No library item builds a personal development plan for a leader or debriefs 360 feedback results
No library item matches mentors to mentees, writes mentor and mentee guides or builds mentoring surveys
No library item writes sign-up and reminder messages for an internal programme
No library item coaches managing up, presence in senior meetings or influence without authority
No library item plans a stay conversation or a written improvement plan for an underperformer
